messages:
maria: Heads up — while validating DSAR delete flows in staging we noticed ephemeral keystore rotation + auto-expiring snapshots. Do we need a formal retention-exception for staging artifacts or can we rely on TTL + an immutable audit trail?
ben: if staging never contains production PII and audit trail is durable with restricted access, a retention-exception usually isn't required. But the audit trail must survive key rotation.
liam: critical detail: current delete job removes data and the audit row in same transaction. that's the risky part. Audit must be committed before deletion and live in a non-ephemeral store.
maria: ok. today staging rotates keystore every 12h and snapshot TTL is 48h. Our delete job tickets off a Lambda that wipes files and metadata together.
ben: propose split: (1) audit-writer writes minimal, non-PII event to central audit DB (encrypted with central KMS) and returns an audit_ref, (2) deletion worker consumes audit_ref and deletes resources. Audit must not hold raw proof artifacts.
zara-legal: legal input: we need proof of identity verification for up to 1 year for dispute resolution. Storing a proof pointer + signed verification hash is acceptable; do not store raw documents. Also legal-hold capability required.
liam: noted. Implementation idea: audit schema fields = DSAR_ID, REQUESTER_HASH, ACTION, RESOURCE_ID, OPERATOR, PROOF_REF, PROOF_VERIFIED, TIMESTAMP, CORRELATION_ID, LEGAL_HOLD(false). No PII.
ben: and encryption: audit-store encrypted with kms://central/audit-key, different from staging keystore. RBAC: only sec/legal & audit-service can decrypt. Developers have 'staging-dsar-runner' role that can trigger runs but not read proofs.
dsar-bot: Reminder: proof artifacts must be uploaded to `s3://legal-proofs-staging/` with path `dsar/<DSAR_ID>/<artifact_hash>`. Bot will validate artifact metadata but will not download content.
zara-legal: also require breakglass + 2-person approval for snapshot export from staging into central account for forensic holds. Must be logged and emit an audit event with approver ids.
liam: agree. Proposed runbook: 1) create export request 2) require two approvers (sec + legal or sec + eng leads) 3) snapshot exported to central account with `LEGAL_HOLD=true` 4) notify ops & legal 5) retention subject to manual release.
maria: can we automate the hold-check in purge job? purge should consult `legal_holds` table and skip any DSAR_ID with active hold. also emit metric `staging_dsar_purge{status=blocked|deleted}`.
ben: yes — make purge idempotent and safe to retry. Also ensure audit rows are write-once (append-only) and immutable.
zara-legal: confirm that `PROOF_REF` is only a pointer (s3 path + artifact hash) and that the artifact is encrypted with central KMS and ACLed to legal+sec. Legal needs a small UI to list holds and request releases.
liam: tech notes — example config snippet: ```yaml
audit:
  enabled: true
  pre_delete_commit: true
  encryption: kms://central/audit-key
  fields: [DSAR_ID,REQUESTER_HASH,ACTION,RESOURCE_ID,OPERATOR,PROOF_REF,PROOF_VERIFIED,TIMESTAMP,CORRELATION_ID,LEGAL_HOLD]
staging:
  keystore_ttl: 12h
  snapshot_ttl: 48h
  proofs_bucket: s3://legal-proofs-staging/
```
ben: ops task list: (A) change delete worker to call audit-writer before deletion, (B) create `legal_holds` table and guard purge job, (C) set up central KMS key policy + breakglass flow, (D) add `staging-dsar-runner` role with no audit decryption.
dsar-bot: Created ticket #5034: staging-dsar-audit-runbook. Assigned: liam, ben.
maria: timeline: want end-to-end canary in staging next week. I'll block time to test once PRs are up. @liam @ben please ping when ready.
zara-legal: i'll review hold UX + retention language once tech design is up. Also log retention for audit rows must be at least 2 years for compliance review — verify with privacy.
ben: noted. we'll surface retention policy in PR.
liam: i'll draft the runbook + PR for RBAC + audit schema today; will include unit/integration tests and e2e checklist.
maria: thanks everyone. If no objections we'll treat staging as compliant without a formal exception so long as audit-store is durable, proofs are only pointers, and legal-hold exists. :thumbsup:
zara-legal: sounds good pending the runbook and final retention numbers.
